name: London
summary: London began as Londinium, a Roman trading town founded around AD 47 at the lowest bridging point of the Thames. Sacked by Boudica, abandoned by Rome, refounded by Alfred and remade by the Normans, it grew into the capital of England and the heart of the largest empire in history — the most populous city on Earth for much of the 19th century. Bombed in the Blitz and rebuilt, it is today a global capital of finance and culture astride the tidal river that made it.

events.title: Londinium founded
events.body: The Romans establish Londinium as a trading settlement and bridgehead on the Thames soon after the invasion of AD 43.

events.title: Boudica burns Londinium
events.body: The rebel queen Boudica sacks and burns the young town during her revolt against Rome.

events.title: The Roman city wall
events.body: Londinium is enclosed by a great stone wall whose line the City of London still echoes.

events.title: Rome withdraws
events.body: Roman rule in Britain ends and Londinium is largely abandoned to ruin.

events.title: The first St Paul’s
events.body: A cathedral to St Paul is founded on Ludgate Hill as the Saxon trading town of Lundenwic grows to the west.

events.title: Alfred refounds London
events.body: Alfred the Great retakes the ruined Roman city from the Vikings and re-establishes it within the old walls.

events.title: The Norman Conquest
events.body: William the Conqueror is crowned in Westminster Abbey; London submits and keeps its ancient liberties.

events.title: The White Tower
events.body: William begins the Tower of London to guard — and overawe — the city.

events.title: Magna Carta
events.body: London’s support helps force King John to seal Magna Carta; the City’s rights are confirmed.

events.title: The Black Death
events.body: Plague arrives in England and kills perhaps half of London’s people.

events.title: The Peasants' Revolt
events.body: Rebels led by Wat Tyler storm London and the Tower before the rising is crushed.

events.title: The Tudor age begins
events.body: Henry VII’s victory at Bosworth begins the Tudor century; London flourishes as a trading capital.

events.title: The Globe Theatre
events.body: Shakespeare’s company opens the Globe on Bankside, heart of London’s theatre boom.

events.title: The Gunpowder Plot
events.body: Guy Fawkes is caught beneath Parliament in a plot to blow up king and Lords.

events.title: The king is executed
events.body: Charles I is beheaded outside the Banqueting House at the climax of the Civil War.

events.title: The Great Plague
events.body: The last great outbreak of bubonic plague kills nearly a quarter of Londoners.

events.title: The Great Fire
events.body: A fire starting in Pudding Lane destroys medieval London, including old St Paul’s.

events.title: Wren’s St Paul’s
events.body: Christopher Wren’s great domed cathedral is completed, crowning the rebuilt City.

events.title: Georgian London
events.body: Under the Hanoverians London spreads west into elegant garden squares.

events.title: Parliament burns
events.body: Fire destroys the old Palace of Westminster; the Gothic Houses of Parliament rise in its place.

events.title: The Great Exhibition
events.body: The Crystal Palace showcases the world’s manufactures at the height of empire.

events.title: The Underground
events.body: The world’s first underground railway opens beneath London.

events.title: The Whitechapel murders
events.body: The unsolved “Jack the Ripper” killings horrify the crowded East End.

events.title: The largest city on Earth
events.body: At Queen Victoria’s death London is the biggest and richest city in the world.

events.title: The Blitz
events.body: German bombing devastates London for months; the city endures night after night.

events.title: Windrush and the Games
events.body: Postwar London hosts the Olympics and welcomes Caribbean migrants who reshape the city.

events.title: Mayor and Millennium
events.body: London elects its first citywide mayor and marks the millennium with the Eye and Tate Modern.

events.title: The 7/7 bombings
events.body: Suicide bombers attack the transport network, killing 52 people.

events.title: London 2012
events.body: London becomes the first city to host the modern Olympic Games three times.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.

dynasties.note: Dynasties and houses that shaped London.

list.name: House of Plantagenet
list.legacy: The Tower, Westminster and English common law
list.summary: The kings who built the Tower and Westminster and shaped English common law, ruling from London through the Middle Ages.

list.name: House of Tudor
list.legacy: The English Reformation and a European capital
list.summary: Henry VIII and Elizabeth I broke with Rome and made London a great European capital of trade and theatre.

list.name: The City of London Corporation
list.summary: The livery companies and ancient Corporation gave the City a self-rule and mercantile power that outlasted kings.

list.name: The Rothschilds
list.legacy: London as a capital of global finance
list.summary: N. M. Rothschild & Sons helped make 19th-century London the hub of world finance.
